2. Five Neutral Powers. The Court shall take cognisance only of inter-state litigation; nevertheless, a state may lay before the Court a suit based upon rights which it claims to put forward on behalf of one of its citizens against another state. (art. 20).
3. Interparliamentary Union. The Court is open to deal with conflicts between private persons and foreign states and between private persons. (art. 2).
4. International Law Union. It follows from art. 1 that the Court has jurisdiction only over conflicts between states.
